Origin: Fully synthetic fictional airport scenario. Not a historical FAA report, not the private FAA audit, and not a claim about a real airport.

Briefing.Title: Synthetic Harbor County Airport router fault
Briefing.Body: Fictional scenario for model evaluation only. At Harbor County Airport, an equipment upgrade on Tuesday, April 7, 2026 caused a communications outage lasting 42 minutes. The airport paused all departures as a precaution. Exactly 18 departures were delayed. No aircraft crashed and no passenger injuries were reported. The initial review attributed the outage to a misconfigured router, NOT a cyberattack. The old copper cables were NOT replaced during this work. The airport completed a verified repair BEFORE departures resumed.

Profiles.Name: Arthur
Profiles.Persona: A retired machinist in his seventies. He spent 40 years on a factory floor. He has no children, has never worked for an airport, and has never held a pilot license. He speaks bluntly and uses mechanical analogies.

Profiles.Name: Maya
Profiles.Persona: A hospice nurse in her thirties whose father retrained after a mill closure. She has never worked for the FAA or in aviation. She values safety and the ability to retrain.

Profiles.Name: Daniel
Profiles.Persona: A high-school shop teacher in his fifties. He has never held a pilot license and has never piloted any aircraft. He is skeptical of corporate promises and teaches practical safety.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur
Cases.Candidate: Shiny pipes don't fix rusted foundations.
Cases.Rationale: A metaphor, not a claim that this airport had literal rusted pipes.

Cases.Speaker: Maya
Cases.Candidate: If the highway lights went out during rush hour, we'd stop the cars until it was safe.
Cases.Rationale: A hypothetical road analogy, not a source claim.

Cases.Speaker: Daniel
Cases.Candidate: I think the airport took too long to decide, even if the stop itself was necessary.
Cases.Rationale: An opinion about timeliness, not a contradiction of the briefing.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur
Cases.Candidate: What if the router had failed again the very next day? Would we be prepared?
Cases.Rationale: An explicitly hypothetical question.

Cases.Speaker: Maya
Cases.Candidate: Safety matters more to me than punctuality, even if people hate waiting.
Cases.Rationale: A subjective value judgment.

Cases.Speaker: Daniel
Cases.Candidate: That router deserves a vacation, just not anywhere near an airport.
Cases.Rationale: Humor without an asserted event.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur
Cases.Candidate: I once repaired a stubborn lathe in the middle of a rainstorm.
Cases.Rationale: Plausible self-authored fiction that does not conflict with the synthetic profile.

Cases.Speaker: Maya
Cases.Candidate: Daniel, I think your approach puts too much faith in technology and not enough in people.

Prior.Speaker: Daniel
Prior.Text: Better diagnostics are the first thing I would fund.

Cases.Rationale: Ordinary disagreement with another participant.

Cases.Speaker: Daniel
Cases.Candidate: Did the report say whether a technician had been working overnight? I don't remember seeing that.
Cases.Rationale: A question that explicitly does not assert a new fact.

Cases.Speaker: Daniel
Cases.Candidate: In my workshop, I wouldn't let a student use a saw if the guard had fallen off.
Cases.Rationale: A hypothetical practice comparison from an educator.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur
Cases.Candidate: Maybe somebody rushed the installation, but I can't say from this report.
Cases.Rationale: Clearly labeled speculation rather than source attribution.

Cases.Speaker: Maya
Cases.Candidate: I'd rather miss a connection than wonder whether a radar feed is reliable.
Cases.Rationale: A personal preference.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur
Cases.Candidate: Was it eighteen delayed departures? I might be remembering that number wrong.
Cases.Rationale: A tentative recollection, not a falsified definitive statistic.

Cases.Speaker: Daniel
Cases.Candidate: Next time I'd ask for a public status board showing when the network has been tested.
Cases.Rationale: A proposal, not a claim about the past.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur
Cases.Candidate: We shouldn't let a faulty router stay in service until it's tested properly.

Prior.Speaker: Arthur
Prior.Text: Until they've tested that broken router, I wouldn't put it back into service.

Cases.Rationale: Prior message expresses similar point, but these are not exact copies and M1b isn't a stagnation gate.

Cases.Speaker: Maya
Cases.Candidate: The safer course is to delay a departure rather than gamble with a bad signal.

Prior.Speaker: Daniel
Prior.Text: I'd keep the airplanes on the ground while those signals are unreliable.

Cases.Rationale: Meaning resembles Daniel's prior message, but not a verbatim copy.

Cases.Speaker: Daniel
Cases.Candidate: A routine upgrade still needs an independent check afterward.

Prior.Speaker: Daniel
Prior.Text: Even routine maintenance should be checked by somebody else.

Cases.Rationale: Similar argument, not identical language or an identity/fact violation.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur
Cases.Candidate: Forty-two minutes was costly, but it beats taking off with an unreliable system.

Prior.Speaker: Maya
Prior.Text: Delaying departures is expensive, but flying with bad data would be worse.

Cases.Rationale: Echoes earlier concern while contributing a duration and a tradeoff.

Cases.Candidate: The report confirms an aircraft crashed during the outage.
Cases.Rationale: The fictional briefing explicitly says there was no crash.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur

Cases.Speaker: Maya

Cases.Rationale: The briefing says departures were paused during the outage.

Cases.Speaker: Daniel
Cases.Candidate: Several passengers were injured in the incident, the report says.
Cases.Rationale: The briefing says no injuries were reported.

Cases.Speaker: Arthur
Cases.Candidate: They resumed departures before anyone had verified the repair.
Cases.Rationale: The briefing says the repair was verified before departures resumed.

Cases.Candidate: Arthur said there were 140 delayed departures.

Prior.Speaker: Daniel
Prior.Text: The report lists exactly 18 delayed departures.

Cases.Rationale: The prior speaker was Daniel, and the quoted figure was 18.
